note: Figures are read from each scientist's public Google Scholar profile. pipeline/update_metrics.py refreshes them on the first of each month; if a profile cannot be read, the previous figures stay with their date.

scientists.name: Robert D. Hare
scientists.blurb: The world's leading authority on psychopathy and author of the Hare Psychopathy Checklist-Revised (PCL-R), the main tool researchers and clinicians use to assess psychopathic traits.

scientists.name: Paul J. Frick
scientists.blurb: A leading authority on callous-unemotional traits (the precursors of psychopathic traits) in children.

scientists.name: Adrian Raine
scientists.blurb: A top researcher in psychopathy whose work also covers antisocial behavior generally and criminal behavior in particular.

scientists.name: R. James R. Blair
scientists.blurb: A noted authority on psychopathy and anxiety disorders, and the author of the Violence Inhibition Mechanism model.

scientists.name: Kent A. Kiehl
scientists.affiliation: Mind Research Network and University of New Mexico
scientists.blurb: Author of The Psychopath Whisperer: The Science of Those Without Conscience. Dr. Kiehl specializes in the neuroscience of psychopathy.

scientists.name: Essi Viding
scientists.blurb: Professor of Developmental Psychopathology at University College London, where she co-directs the Developmental Risk and Resilience Unit.

scientists.name: Joseph P. Newman
scientists.blurb: Best known for his research on attentional processes in psychopathy.

scientists.name: Eva R. Kimonis
scientists.affiliation: University of New South Wales, Sydney
scientists.blurb: Studies the development, assessment and treatment of psychopathic traits and aggressive behavior in youth, with special interest in childhood maltreatment and deficits in emotional processing.

scientists.name: Andrea L. Glenn
scientists.blurb: Psychologist at the University of Alabama, with a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and a degree in neuroscience and behavioral biology from Emory University.
